mainTopic: ערלה and כלאים outside ארץ ישראל: doubtful versus certain ערלה, רבי יוחנן's הלכה למשה מסיני, and which kinds of כלאים apply outside the land
overview: The amud opens by fixing the wording of an earlier teaching about doubtful ערלה outside ארץ ישראל: both cases should read 'buys' or both 'gathers.' Next come stories of אמוראים who ate doubtful ערלה only when someone else supplied it, and the view of the scholars of פומבדיתא that there is no ערלה outside the land at all. רבי יוחנן fiercely rejects that view, and the גמרא traces it to רבי אליעזר הגדול, reading his words in the משנה as 'חדש' instead of 'even חדש.' רבי יוחנן then teaches that ערלה outside the land is a הלכה למשה מסיני, and that הלכה itself permits doubtful fruit and forbids certain ערלה. He also says there is Torah-level מלקות for כלאים outside the land. The גמרא explains that this means grafting trees, which שמואל derives from the פסוק as applying everywhere, while mixing seeds is limited to ארץ ישראל. Stories of רב חנן, רב ענן and רב יוסף show these rules in practice. The amud ends as רב יוסף retracts based on רב's garden planted in rows, and אביי begins to push back, a point that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why does the teaching use two different words?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why one case says 'goes down and buys' and the other says 'goes down and gathers.' It should use the same wording for both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the teaching say either 'In both cases he may go down and buy,' or 'In both cases he may go down and gather'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the earlier teaching uses different wording for two cases that seem to follow the same rule. It asks why the wording is not the same for both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One case says the person may 'buy' the produce and the other says he may 'gather' it. If the law is the same in both, the different words look strange. Either both should say 'buy' or both should say 'gather.'

keyTerms.meaning: Let it teach / it should have taught
This and that, meaning both cases
Goes down (into the field) and buys
Goes down (into the field) and gathers

phrases.english: Let it teach either:
'In both this and that case, one goes down and buys,'
or: 'In both this and that case, one goes down and gathers'!

steps.triggerLanguage: נִיתְנֵי אוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the teaching discussed just before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The different wording ('buys' and 'gathers') used for the two cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the law is the same, the wording should be the same.

steps.title: שמואל told רב ענן to read both cases the same way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל already told רב ענן to correct the wording so that both cases match.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't שמואל say to רב ענן: Teach it either as 'In both cases he goes down and buys' or as 'In both cases he goes down and gathers'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting שמואל. He agreed the wording should match and told רב ענן to fix it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer accepts the challenge. The text really should be read the same way in both cases. שמואל's instruction shows the uneven wording was not meant to teach a difference.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't (he) say? Used to bring a known statement as an answer

phrases.english: But didn't שמואל say to רב ענן:
Teach either: 'In both this and that case, one goes down and buys'
or: 'In both this and that case, one goes down and gathers.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאָמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב עָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the point and corrects the text based on שמואל's instruction
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The different words seemed to show a different law for each case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The text should be read the same way in both cases, either 'buys' or 'gathers.'

steps.title: מר בריה דרבנא's lenient reading
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרבנא read the teaching the lenient way: in both cases one may go down and gather, as long as he does not pick with his own hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר, son of רבנא, taught it the lenient way: 'In both cases one goes down and gathers, as long as he does not pick by hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא gives his own reading of the same text, and it is the more lenient one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Of שמואל's two choices, this reading picks 'gathers' for both cases, which allows more than just buying. The only limit is that the Jew may not pick the fruit with his own hand.

keyTerms.meaning: In the lenient way
As long as / provided that
By hand

phrases.aramaic: מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבְנָא מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ לְקוּלָּא:
phrases.english: מר, son of רבנא, taught it leniently:
'In both this and that case, one goes down and gathers,
provided that he does not pick by hand.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבְנָא מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ לְקוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a specific, lenient choice between the two readings allowed in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both cases read 'goes down and gathers,' as long as he does not pick by hand.
steps.whatToRemember: The wording question ends with matching readings for both cases. The lenient version is 'gathers, but not by his own hand.'

steps.title: לוי asks שמואל to supply him
steps.stepSummary: לוי told שמואל to supply him with doubtful ערלה produce, and he would eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי said to שמואל: 'אריוך, supply me, and I will eat.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: how אמוראים actually behaved with doubtful ערלה outside ארץ ישראל. לוי is willing to eat it as long as someone else hands it to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Doubtful ערלה outside ארץ ישראל is allowed if the person does not take it himself. So לוי asks שמואל to give it to him, and then he may eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: A nickname for שמואל
Supply me / provide for me
Fruit from a tree's first three years, which is forbidden

phrases.english: לוי said to שמואל:
אריוך, supply me, and I will eat.
phrases.notes: He means: you hand me the doubtful fruit, so I am not taking it myself, and then I can eat it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לֵוִי לִשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the wording question to how אמוראים practiced the leniency.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Doubtful ערלה outside ארץ ישראל may be eaten if another person supplies it.

steps.title: Two אמוראים supply each other
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא and רבה בר רב חנן would supply doubtful ערלה produce to each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אויא and רבה בר רב חנן would supply each other.
steps.whatsHappening: Another example of the same practice. Each of them handed doubtful fruit to the other so that neither took it for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works the same way as לוי's request. The fruit is allowed only if someone else provides it, so the two of them simply swapped roles.

keyTerms.meaning: They would supply
To each other

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַוְיָא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב חָנָן
phrases.english: רב אויא and רבה בר רב חנן
would supply each other.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַוְיָא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב חָנָן מְסַפְּקוּ סַפּוֹקֵי לַהֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second example of the practice from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Supplying each other doubtful ערלה is allowed.

steps.title: The scholars of פומבדיתא: no ערלה outside ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The sharp scholars of פומבדיתא said there is no ערלה outside ארץ ישראל at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sharp scholars of פומבדיתא said: There is no ערלה outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: A much more extreme view is brought. Some scholars said the ערלה prohibition does not apply outside ארץ ישראל at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 4 and 5 allowed only doubtful fruit, and only if someone else gave it. This view goes much further: even fruit that is certainly ערלה would be allowed outside ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: The sharp scholars of פומבדיתא
Outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: The sharp scholars of פומבדיתא said:
There is no ערלה outside ארץ ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי חֲרִיפֵי דְפוּמְבְּדִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes much further than the limited leniency of steps 4 and 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ערלה prohibition does not apply outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with steps 4 and 5. They allowed only doubtful fruit. This view says even certain ערלה is allowed outside ארץ ישראל, and רבי יוחנן rejects it next.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's sharp response
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה sent the question to רבי יוחנן. He answered: keep the leniency on doubtful fruit quiet, forbid certain ערלה, announce that such fruit must be buried, and he cursed anyone who says there is no ערלה outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה sent the question to רבי יוחנן. He sent back: 'Keep the doubtful case quiet, destroy the certain case, and announce that their fruit must be buried. Whoever says there is no ערלה outside ארץ ישראל will have no child or grandchild "who casts a line by lot in the congregation of ה׳."'
steps.whatsHappening: The question goes to רבי יוחנן in ארץ ישראל. He strongly rejects the view of פומבדיתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן agrees that doubtful fruit is allowed, but he says not to publicize it. Certain ערלה is fully forbidden, and fruit of people who are lenient with it must be buried. His curse shows how seriously he rejects the view that there is no ערלה outside ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: Keep the doubtful case quiet (don't publicize the leniency)
Destroy the certain case (treat it as fully forbidden)
Must be buried / put away so no one benefits
Child and grandchild

phrases.aramaic: שַׁלְחַהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן.
phrases.english: רב יהודה sent it before רבי יוחנן.
He sent to him: Keep its doubtful case closed,
phrases.notes: Doubtful fruit really is allowed, but don't spread that around.

phrases.english: and destroy its certain case,
and announce about their fruits that they must be buried.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הָאוֹמֵר אֵין עׇרְלָה בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ –
phrases.english: And whoever says there is no ערלה outside ארץ ישראל –
shall have no child or grandchild,
'who casts a line by lot in the congregation of ה׳.'

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁלְחַהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strongly rejects the view of פומבדיתא from step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Doubtful ערלה outside ארץ ישראל is allowed but should not be publicized. Certain ערלה is forbidden, and fruit of those who are lenient with it must be buried.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule: ערלה applies outside ארץ ישראל, with a quiet leniency only for doubtful cases.
steps.whatToRemember: Outside ארץ ישראל, doubtful ערלה is allowed (keep it quiet) and certain ערלה is forbidden. Saying 'no ערלה outside ארץ ישראל' is sharply condemned.

steps.title: Whom did the scholars of פומבדיתא follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which earlier authority the scholars of פומבדיתא were relying on.
steps.simpleTranslation: And whose opinion did they follow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its next move by asking where the view of פומבדיתא came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן rejected the view so strongly that the גמרא wants to know whether it had any earlier source at all. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom / following whose view
They held it

phrases.english: And they, like whom did they hold?
phrases.notes: 'They' means the sharp scholars of פומבדיתא from a few lines back.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִינְהוּ כְּמַאן סַבְרוּהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the פומבדיתא view of step 6 to find its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The earlier source for the view that there is no ערלה outside ארץ ישראל

steps.title: The source: a ברייתא from רבי אליעזר הגדול
steps.stepSummary: They followed a ברייתא passed down through a long chain of names back to רבי אליעזר הגדול, who said there is no ערלה outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אלעזר son of רבי יוסי says in the name of רבי יוסי בן דורמסקית, who said in the name of רבי יוסי הגלילי, who said in the name of רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who said in the name of רבי אליעזר הגדול: There is no ערלה outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the scholars of פומבדיתא relied on a ברייתא. Its chain of teachers goes back to רבי אליעזר הגדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The view of פומבדיתא was not made up. It has a תנאי source passed down through a chain of five teachers, starting from רבי אליעזר הגדול. That shows it is a real opinion, even though רבי יוחנן rejected it.

keyTerms.meaning: Like what was taught in a ברייתא
In the name of

phrases.english: Like that which was taught:
רבי אלעזר son of רבי יוסי says
in the name of רבי יוסי בן דורמסקית,
who said in the name of רבי יוסי הגלילי,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי,
phrases.english: who said in the name of רבי יוחנן בן נורי,
who said in the name of רבי אליעזר the Great:
There is no ערלה outside ארץ ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They followed a ברייתא in the name of רבי אליעזר הגדול that there is no ערלה outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatToRemember: The view of פומבדיתא goes back to רבי אליעזר הגדול, but רבי יוחנן firmly rejected it in practice.

steps.title: Challenge: Doesn't the משנה show רבי אליעזר holds ערלה applies outside the land?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי אליעזר could hold there is no ערלה outside ארץ ישראל, since the משנה quotes him saying 'even חדש,' which assumes ערלה and כלאים do apply there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it doesn't apply? But we learned in the משנה: רבי אליעזר says, 'Even the new crop!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from Step 9, which said רבי אליעזר holds there is no ערלה outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists ערלה and כלאים as applying outside ארץ ישראל, and then רבי אליעזר adds 'even חדש.' The word 'even' means he agrees with the list and adds one more item. So he must hold that ערלה applies outside the land, which contradicts the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in a משנה)? This opens a challenge from a משנה.
Even, also. It adds something on top of what was already said.
New grain that may not be eaten before the עומר is brought.

steps.confusionAlert: The whole challenge rests on the one small word 'אף' (even). Without that word, there would be no question.

phrases.english: But does it not apply?
phrases.notes: He means: does רבי אליעזר really say ערלה doesn't apply outside ארץ ישראל?

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in the משנה:
Rabbi Eliezer says: Even the new crop!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא? וְהָאֲנַן תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא cited in Step 9 as the source for the scholars of פומבדיתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא saying רבי אליעזר holds there is no ערלה outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's 'even חדש' shows רבי אליעזר agrees that ערלה and כלאים apply outside the land.

steps.title: Answer: Read the משנה as 'חדש,' not 'even חדש'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording of the משנה: רבי אליעזר says only 'חדש' applies outside the land, not 'even חדש.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach it as: 'the new crop.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing the wording of the משנה and taking out the word 'even.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without 'אף,' רבי אליעזר is no longer adding to the list. He is replacing it. In his view only חדש applies outside ארץ ישראל, which fits the ברייתא that he holds there is no ערלה outside the land.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the corrected wording, רבי אליעזר holds that only חדש applies outside ארץ ישראל, not ערלה or כלאים. That is the basis for the scholars of פומבדיתא.

phrases.english: Teach: "The new crop."
phrases.notes: Drop the word 'even.' Now רבי אליעזר is saying only חדש applies outside the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה reads 'even חדש,' so רבי אליעזר agrees that ערלה applies outside the land.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה should read just 'חדש,' so רבי אליעזר limits the rule outside the land to חדש only.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: ערלה outside the land is a הלכה למשה מסיני
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי quotes רבי יוחנן that the prohibition of ערלה outside ארץ ישראל comes from a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: ערלה outside ארץ ישראל is a law given to משה at סיני.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement explains where the prohibition of ערלה outside the land comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No פסוק says ערלה applies outside the land, but רבי יוחנן says it is an oral law handed down from משה at סיני. That explains why רבי יוחנן cursed anyone who denies ערלה outside the land in Step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: A law given orally to משה at סיני, not written in a פסוק.
Outside ארץ ישראל.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi says that Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
Orla outside of the Land
is a law given to Moses from Sinai.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי יוחנן's strict stance on ערלה outside the land from Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ערלה outside ארץ ישראל is forbidden because of a הלכה למשה מסיני.

steps.title: רבי זירא: A ברייתא is lenient on doubtful ערלה outside the land
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא challenges רבי אסי from a ברייתא that permits doubtful ערלה in סוריא and lets one gather it outside the land. That seems too lenient for a law from סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רבי אסי: But it was taught in a ברייתא: Doubtful ערלה in ארץ ישראל is forbidden, in סוריא it is permitted, and outside the land one may go down and pick it!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges the statement that ערלה outside the land is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A law from סיני is like a Torah law, and with Torah laws we are strict when in doubt. Yet the ברייתא is lenient on doubtful ערלה outside the land, and it even allows going and picking it. That suggests the prohibition there is weaker than a law from סיני.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt, a case where we are unsure.
Syria, an area with an in-between status, not fully ארץ ישראל.
He goes down and picks it, meaning he may take the fruit himself.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Asi:
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
Uncertain orla in the Land is forbidden,
in Syria it is permitted,
outside the Land one goes down and gathers it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי אַסִּי: וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's statement in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ערלה outside the land is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A law from סיני should be treated strictly when in doubt, but the ברייתא is lenient on doubtful fruit outside the land.

steps.title: Answer: The הלכה itself said doubtful is permitted and certain is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: After a moment of stunned silence, רבי אסי answers that the הלכה למשה מסיני was given with this built-in rule: doubtful ערלה outside the land is permitted, and certain ערלה is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was stunned for a moment. Then he said to him: Say that this is how it was given: its doubt is permitted, and its certainty is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי answers רבי זירא's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leniency on doubtful fruit is not a sign that the prohibition is weak. The law from סיני itself was given with that condition. So it fits the ruling in Step 7: keep the leniency on doubtful fruit quiet, but forbid certain ערלה.

keyTerms.meaning: He was stunned or speechless.
Say, read it this way.
Certain, a case where we know for sure.

steps.whatToRemember: ערלה outside ארץ ישראל is a הלכה למשה מסיני, and that same הלכה permits doubtful fruit and forbids certain ערלה.

phrases.english: "He was dismayed for a while"
He said to him: Say it was stated like this:

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא כָּךְ נֶאֶמְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves רבי זירא's challenge in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining what the law actually contains
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A law from סיני must be strict even in cases of doubt.
steps.terutzMaskana: This הלכה was given with the leniency built in: doubtful fruit is permitted and certain ערלה is forbidden.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: One gets מלקות for כלאים outside the land by Torah law
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי quotes רבי יוחנן that a person who violates כלאים outside ארץ ישראל is given מלקות on a Torah level.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: We give lashes for כלאים, by Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement says that כלאים outside the land is a Torah prohibition that carries מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מלקות is given only for a Torah prohibition. So רבי יוחנן is saying that כלאים outside ארץ ישראל is from the Torah, not just from the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: We give lashes (מלקות).
Forbidden mixtures of species, in plants or animals.
By Torah law.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi says that Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
One is flogged for diverse kinds by Torah law.
phrases.notes: The topic is still outside ארץ ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לוֹקִין עַל הַכִּלְאַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from ערלה to כלאים, the other item the משנה lists as applying outside the land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Violating כלאים outside the land brings Torah-level מלקות.

steps.title: Challenge: A משנה says כלאים outside the land is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי challenges this from a משנה that says כלאים outside the land is מדברי סופרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי said to him: But we learned in a משנה: כלאים is from the words of the סופרים!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי challenges רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If כלאים outside the land is only rabbinic, there can be no Torah-level מלקות for it. That directly contradicts רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: From the words of the scribes, meaning a rabbinic law.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Yosei, said to him:
But didn't we learn in a משנה:
Diverse kinds are by rabbinic law!
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in ערלה 3:9, which is talking about outside the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי: וְהָאֲנַן תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that there is Torah-level מלקות for כלאים outside the land.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה says כלאים outside the land is only rabbinic, so there can be no Torah-level מלקות.

steps.title: Answer: Vineyard mixtures are rabbinic, grafting trees is from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא splits the cases: the משנה means כלאי הכרם, which is rabbinic outside the land, while רבי יוחנן means grafting one tree onto another species, which is from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here it is talking about mixtures in a vineyard, and there it is talking about grafting a tree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying each source is talking about a different kind of כלאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is more than one type of כלאים. כלאי הכרם outside the land is only rabbinic, so the משנה is right about that type. Grafting trees is forbidden by the Torah everywhere, so רבי יוחנן's מלקות applies to that type.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This opens an answer that splits the cases.
Planting grain or vegetables together with grapevines.
Grafting a tree onto a different species.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't conclude that כלאים 'isn't' a Torah law outside the land. One type (grafting) is from the Torah there, while another type (the vineyard) is rabbinic there.

phrases.english: It is not difficult.
Here it is referring to diverse kinds in a vineyard,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the משנה, which calls it rabbinic.

phrases.english: there it is referring to grafting a tree.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן בְּכִלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם, כָּאן בְּהַרְכָּבַת הָאִילָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of Step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All כלאים outside the land is the same, so the משנה and רבי יוחנן clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: Vineyard כלאים outside the land is rabbinic, and grafting trees is a Torah prohibition that carries מלקות.

steps.title: Support from שמואל: These mixing laws were given before מתן תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this fits שמואל, who reads 'את חקתי תשמרו' as 'statutes I already engraved for you,' meaning the laws of mixing animals and grafting were already given before מתן תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like שמואל, who said: 'My statutes you shall keep.' These are statutes I already engraved for you: 'Do not let your animals mate with a different kind; do not sow your field with mixed seeds.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the answer in Step 17 with a teaching of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל reads the word 'חקתי' as laws that were already 'engraved' before the Torah was given. That means these mixing laws were never tied to the land of ישראל in the first place. So it makes sense that grafting is forbidden by the Torah even outside the land.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with שמואל's view.
My statutes.
That I engraved or set in place.
Do not let animals of different kinds mate.

steps.whyThisMatters: It gives the reason why grafting is from the Torah everywhere: the law was set before מתן תורה, so it was never tied to the land.

phrases.english: As Shmuel taught, for Shmuel says:
"You shall keep My statutes"
statutes that I already engraved for you,
"You shall not let your cattle mate with a diverse kind;
you shall not sow your field"

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִשְׁמוּאֵל, דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in Step 17 that grafting is a Torah prohibition even outside the land.
steps.raayaObject: Grafting trees is forbidden by the Torah even outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's reading of 'את חקתי תשמרו' (ויקרא 19:19) as laws already given before מתן תורה.

steps.title: Animal mating and field grafting are compared, so both apply everywhere
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק puts 'your animal' next to 'your field'. Just as the animal law is about mating, the field law is about grafting. And just as the animal law applies everywhere, so does grafting.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as 'your animal' means mating two species, 'your field' means grafting one tree onto another. And just as the animal law applies both in ארץ ישראל and outside it, the field law also applies both in the land and outside it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes שמואל's reading of the פסוק by comparing the two halves of the verse. This proves רבי יוחנן's claim that grafting is forbidden from the Torah even outside the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mating animals is a personal act, not a law tied to the land, so it applies everywhere. Because the פסוק pairs it with 'your field', grafting also gets that status. This backs up the answer in Step 17, where רבי יוחנן's מלקות outside the land refers to grafting.

keyTerms.meaning: Mating one animal species with another
Grafting one tree species onto another
'Your field', the field half of the פסוק
Outside ארץ ישראל

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for why grafting is a Torah prohibition even outside ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Just as 'your animal' is about mating,
phrases.notes: Both phrases come from ויקרא 19:19: 'your animal you shall not mate... your field you shall not sow.'

phrases.english: so too 'your field' is about grafting.
And just as 'your animal' applies
both in the land and outside the land,
so too 'your field' applies
both in the land and outside the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה בְּהֶמְתְּךָ בְּהַרְבָּעָה אַף שָׂדְךָ בְּהַרְכָּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes שמואל's reading of the פסוק started in Step 18
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling (Step 15, as explained in Step 17) that grafting outside the land carries Torah מלקות
steps.raayaSupportSource: The pairing of 'your animal' and 'your field' in ויקרא 19:19, read through שמואל's approach

steps.title: Challenge: the word 'your field' suggests the land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that 'your field' sounds like a field in ארץ ישראל, so how can grafting apply outside the land?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the פסוק says 'your field'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the conclusion it just reached. The word 'field' seems to point to land-based laws, which normally apply only in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Laws that depend on a field usually count as מצוות התלויות בארץ. So 'your field' looks like it limits the law to the land, which would contradict the derivation in Step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But it is written!', used to raise a challenge from a פסוק

phrases.english: But it is written: 'your field'!
phrases.notes: The point is that 'your field' sounds like your own field in ארץ ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא הָכְתִיב שָׂדְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of Step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the field prohibition applies outside the land
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Your field' implies a land-based law, and land-based laws apply only in ארץ ישראל

steps.title: 'Your field' only leaves out mixed seeds outside the land
steps.stepSummary: The word 'your field' teaches that planting mixed seeds is not forbidden outside the land. It does not limit grafting.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word comes to exclude mixed seeds outside the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'your field' has a narrower job. It leaves out planting mixed seeds outside ארץ ישראל, while grafting stays forbidden everywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse covers two kinds of field mixing, grafting and sowing seeds. The comparison to animals teaches that grafting applies everywhere. The word 'your field' limits only seed-mixing to the land.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude
Seeds, here meaning כלאי זרעים, planting different seeds together

steps.whatToRemember: Grafting is forbidden from the Torah everywhere. Mixing seeds is forbidden only in ארץ ישראל.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up grafting (הרכבה) with planting seeds together (כלאי זרעים). They have different rules outside the land.

phrases.english: That comes to exclude seeds
that are outside the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא לְמַעוֹטֵי זְרָעִים שֶׁבְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the word to a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Your field' limits all field mixing to ארץ ישראל
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Your field' excludes only seed-mixing outside the land, and grafting applies everywhere

steps.title: Story: a man sowing mixed seeds, and they decide not to punish him
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן and רב ענן see a man sowing mixed seeds. One wants to put him in נידוי, and the other says he doesn't understand the הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן and רב ענן were walking on the road. They saw a man sowing different seeds together. One said: 'Come, let's put him in נידוי.' The other said: 'You are not clear on this.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows Step 21 in real life. Sowing mixed seeds outside ארץ ישראל is permitted, so there is no reason to punish the man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rabbi who wanted נידוי treated mixed seeds as forbidden everywhere. The other rabbi corrected him, because 'your field' excludes seeds outside the land.

keyTerms.meaning: Were walking along
Let us put him in שמתא, a ban
'It is not clear to you', literally 'not white to you'

phrases.english: רב חנן and רב ענן
were walking along on the road.
They saw a certain man
who was sowing seeds together with each other.
One said to the other: Let the master come, let us ban him.
He said to him: You are not clear on this.
phrases.notes: He means that, as the last line taught, mixing seeds outside the land is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חָנָן וְרַב עָנָן הֲווֹ שָׁקְלִי וְאָזְלִי בְּאוֹרְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Story showing the rule of Step 21 in practice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No נידוי for sowing mixed seeds outside the land, because it is permitted there

steps.title: Second scene: a man planting wheat and barley among vines
steps.stepSummary: The two rabbis see another man planting wheat and barley between grapevines. One again suggests putting him in נידוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: They also saw a man sowing wheat and barley between grapevines. One said: 'Come, let's put him in נידוי.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues with a harder case, כלאי הכרם. This step sets up the second rabbi's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mixing in a vineyard is more serious than mixing seeds, so this time the call for נידוי seems stronger. The answer comes in Step 24.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore, again
Wheat and barley
Among the grapevines

phrases.english: And again, they saw a certain man

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָא זָרַע חִטֵּי וּשְׂעָרֵי בֵּי גוּפְנֵי.
phrases.english: who was sowing wheat and barley among the grapevines.
One said to the other: Let the master come, let us ban him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ חַזְיוּהּ לְהָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּקָא זָרַע חִטֵּי וּשְׂעָרֵי בֵּי גוּפְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second scene in the same story
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case of planting grain among vines and the proposal of נידוי

steps.title: No ban, because we follow רבי יאשיה's strict definition
steps.stepSummary: The second rabbi rejects the נידוי. According to רבי יאשיה, the Torah violation needs wheat, barley, and a grape seed sown in one throw.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: 'You are not clear on this. Don't we hold like רבי יאשיה, who says a person is not liable until he sows wheat, barley, and a grape seed in one throw of the hand?'
steps.whatsHappening: The second rabbi turns down the call for נידוי again. This man did not meet רבי יאשיה's definition of the Torah violation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה holds that כלאי הכרם is a Torah violation only when two grains and a grape seed are sown together in one motion. Planting grain next to vines that already exist does not meet that definition. So the man's act was not serious enough to deserve נידוי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not bright to you', meaning you are not clear on this
We hold, this is our accepted ruling
A grape seed
In one throw of the hand

steps.whatToRemember: Mixed seeds outside the land are permitted. Grain among vines is a Torah violation only under רבי יאשיה's strict conditions, so neither man deserved נידוי.

phrases.english: He said to him: You are not clear on this,

phrases.aramaic: לָא קַיְימָא לַן כְּרַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה דְּאָמַר:
phrases.english: don't we hold like רבי יאשיה, who says:
not until he sows wheat, barley, and a grape seed
in one throw of the hand?!

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צָהֲרִיתוּ לָא קַיְימָא לַן כְּרַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proposal to ban the man who planted grain among vines

steps.title: רב יוסף mixes seeds and plants them
steps.stepSummary: A story: רב יוסף was mixing different kinds of seeds and planting them, outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף used to mix different seeds together and plant them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about how רב יוסף acted. This sets up אביי's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף lived in בבל, outside ארץ ישראל. By planting mixed seeds he shows that he holds כלאי זרעים is fully permitted outside the land. This fits Step 21, where 'your field' taught that mixed seeds are not forbidden outside the land.

keyTerms.meaning: Mixing together
Seeds (Aramaic)
Planted / sowed

phrases.english: Rav Yosef was mixing seeds and planting them.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, רב יוסף planted mixed seeds outside ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: אביי objects from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף how he can plant mixed seeds, since the משנה teaches that כלאים outside the land is forbidden by the rabbis.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But we learned in the משנה that כלאים is forbidden by the rabbis!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף's practice by quoting the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that outside the land, כלאים is forbidden מדברי סופרים, meaning by rabbinic law. It does not say which kind of כלאים. So it seems to forbid all kinds, including the mixed seeds רב יוסף was planting.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in a משנה)? An opening used to challenge someone
Forbidden mixtures of different species
From the words of the scribes, meaning by rabbinic law

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: But didn't we learn:
Diverse kinds are forbidden by rabbinic law!
phrases.notes: This is the same משנה (ערלה 3:9) that רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי quoted a few lines back. It is talking about what is forbidden outside ארץ ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְהָאֲנַן תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the practice described in Step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's practice of planting mixed seeds outside ארץ ישראל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה forbids כלאים outside the land by rabbinic law and makes no exception. So mixed seeds should also be forbidden.

steps.title: Vineyard mixtures versus seed mixtures
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the משנה means כלאי הכרם. The rabbis made a גזירה outside the land only for vineyard mixtures, because in the land those are forbidden for any benefit. Seed mixtures are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There is no difficulty. The משנה is talking about כלאי הכרם, and I am planting כלאי זרעים. Vineyard mixtures are forbidden for benefit in ארץ ישראל, so the rabbis also made a decree about them outside the land. Seed mixtures are not forbidden for benefit in ארץ ישראל, so the rabbis made no decree about them outside the land.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends himself. He says the משנה is talking about a different kind of כלאים than the kind he is planting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not all כלאים are equally serious. כלאי הכרם is so strict in ארץ ישראל that you may not even benefit from the crop, so the rabbis extended it outside the land. כלאי זרעים in the land only forbids the planting itself, so the rabbis saw no need to extend it outside the land.

Outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: outside the land as well, the rabbis made a decree about them.

phrases.aramaic: כִּלְאֵי זְרָעִים דְּבָאָרֶץ לָא אֲסִירִי בַּהֲנָאָה –

phrases.english: outside the land, the rabbis also made no decree about them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן בְּכִלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם, כָּאן בְּכִלְאֵי זְרָעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from Step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting cases: the משנה refers only to one type of כלאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה forbids every kind of כלאים outside the land.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rabbinic ban outside the land covers only כלאי הכרם, because that mixture is forbidden for benefit in the land. כלאי זרעים outside the land is fully permitted.

steps.title: רב יוסף retracts based on רב's garden
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף takes back what he said. He brings a proof from רב, who planted the study hall's garden in separate rows, apparently to avoid mixing species.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף then said: What I said is not correct. רב planted the garden of the study hall in separate rows. What was the reason? Was it not to avoid mixing כלאים?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף changes his mind. He proves from רב's behavior that even seed mixtures should be avoided outside the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב lived in בבל, outside the land. He carefully planted each species in its own row instead of mixing them. רב יוסף reasons that the only explanation is concern about כלאי זרעים, so seed mixtures must be forbidden outside the land after all.

keyTerms.meaning: He then said / went back and said. Signals a change of mind
It is not correct
Garden
The study hall
Rows / separate beds

phrases.english: Rav Yosef then said:
The thing that I said is not correct,
phrases.notes: He means his claim in Step 27 that seed mixtures are fully allowed outside the land.

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַב זָרַע גִּינְּתָא דְּבֵי רַב מְשָׁארֵי מְשָׁארֵי,
phrases.english: for Rav planted the garden of the study hall in rows and rows.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא – לָאו מִשּׁוּם עֵירוּב עֵירוּבֵי כִלְאַיִם?
phrases.english: What is the reason? Is it not because of mixing diverse kinds?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: לָאו מִלְּתָא הִיא דְּאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב יוסף overturns his own answer from Step 27.
steps.raayaObject: That כלאי זרעים is forbidden outside ארץ ישראל
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's practice of planting the study hall's garden in separate rows

steps.title: אביי begins to push back on the proof
steps.stepSummary: אביי starts to answer רב יוסף with 'בשלמא, if he taught us...'. This is the opening of a rejection of the proof from רב's garden.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: It would make sense if he had taught us...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up אביי's response, which continues right after this. The word בשלמא shows he is about to argue that רב's rows do not prove what רב יוסף wants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי starts with what he would accept: if רב's actions had clearly taught a certain point, the proof would work. The rest of his argument, which comes next, will show why רב's rows do not prove that mixed seeds are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense. Introduces what would work before raising a problem
He taught us / let us know

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: בִּשְׁלָמָא אִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן
phrases.english: Abaye said to him: Granted, if he taught us

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: בִּשְׁלָמָא אִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to answer רב יוסף's proof from Step 28.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from רב's garden (the full argument follows next)
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אביי is about to show that רב's planting in rows does not necessarily teach that mixed seeds are forbidden outside the land.
